title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the sequel to the 'Longue Marche' (pages ~686-687 in Grothendieck's numbering), Grothendieck studies group schemes over a base S_0, roughly Spec of a ring of integers with some primes inverted. These group schemes arise from the arithmetic of low-genus Teichmüller groups. The objects are:
- an 'unimodular' lattice scheme M;
- extensions G^+ of a group H^+ by M, with G^+/M = H^+;
- a group G_{ρ,σ} = O_12^* · G^+, where O_12^* is the unit group scheme of a cyclotomic-type order of conductor 12;
- a canonical character χ: G_{ρ,σ} → O_12^*;
- the normaliser-type subgroup N_ρ = {u : u(ρ) = ρ^{ε_3(u)}}.

The previous page checks that χ restricted to N_ρ is an epimorphism by writing explicit local sections v = σ^{ν_3} δ^{-ν''} u_μ.

This page draws the consequences:
(155) There is an exact sequence 1 → N_ρ^{**} → N_ρ → O_12^* (= γ_{ρ,σ}) → 1, with kernel N_ρ^{**} = Centr_{G^+}(ρ).
(156) H^+_{ρ_0} := G^+/G^° ≅ (H^+)_{ρ_0}, with G^° ≅ M, so H^+ = G^+/M.
(157) There is a canonical map from Z_ρ (the centraliser of ρ in G^+) to Cent_{H^+}(ρ) ≅ L_ρ ≅ (Z/4Z)_{S_0}. It is an epimorphism because the inclusion L_ρ ⊂ Z_ρ gives a section.
(158) Its kernel is Z_ρ° = Z_ρ ∩ M = {x ∈ M : ρ_M x = x}, the scheme of fixed points of ρ on M, i.e. Ker(1 − ρ_M).

Grothendieck then observes that this kernel is not flat. It is zero over S_0 minus {3}, but jumps to dimension 1 in characteristic 3. This happens because det(1 − ρ_M) is divisible by 3: ρ acts on M through a cube/sixth root of unity. He says the 'good' definition of Z_ρ° should instead use the equation (1 − ρ_M)x = 0 in M_∘. In effect this replaces the naive schematic centraliser by its flat closure from the generic part, i.e. restriction away from 3 followed by schematic closure.

The next page carries this out. It obtains a better group N_ρ with 1 → L_ρ → N_ρ → O_12^* → 1, and identifies the image of N_ρ^♮ with the index-2 subgroup of units with ε_3 = 1.

The page serves the construction of well-behaved (flat) group schemes of 'normalisers/centralisers of torsion elements' in arithmetic Teichmüller-type groups. These are presumably used to describe decomposition/inertia data at elliptic points of order 4 and 6.
errors: No genuine mathematical error. Grothendieck himself flags the defect: the naive schematic fixed-point group Ker(1 − ρ_M) is not flat over the base, because the fibre jumps at characteristic 3. He proposes a corrected definition.
Equation numbering is inconsistent with neighbouring pages: (157) and (159) are reused for different formulas on the previous and next pages. This is typical of a draft.

ideas.what: Exact sequence presenting the normaliser N_ρ of a torsion element as an extension of a unit group scheme O_12^* by the centraliser of ρ
ideas.modern_name: normaliser/centraliser exact sequence for group schemes; Weyl-type quotient
ideas.where_published: general formalism in SGA 3; this specific arithmetic setting unpublished

ideas.what: Splitting of centraliser Z_ρ → Cent_{H^+}(ρ) ≅ Z/4Z via the inclusion L_ρ ⊂ Z_ρ; kernel equals the fixed points of ρ on the lattice M
ideas.modern_name: semidirect-product decomposition of centraliser in an extension by a lattice

ideas.what: Observation that the schematic fixed-point group Ker(1 − ρ_M) is non-flat, jumping at p = 3, so the 'right' group is the flat closure of the generic one
ideas.modern_name: flat closure / schematic closure of a group scheme; non-flat fixed-point schemes at bad primes (e.g. at characteristic 3, where j = 0 elliptic curves have extra automorphisms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Raynaud, SGA3 / Bruhat–Tits style flat closures)

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful but routine bookkeeping of group schemes in Grothendieck's unpublished arithmetic study of low-dimensional Teichmüller groups. The only noteworthy point is the explicit attention to non-flatness at the prime 3 and its replacement by a flat closure. That is natural and standard, and no new result or connection is visible on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'D_12^*' should be the unit group scheme \underline{\mathbb{O}}_{12}^* (same symbol as on adjacent pages), equal to γ_{ρ,σ} (lowercase gamma), not Γ_{ρ,σ}.
'Spec \mathbb{Z}_{\rho_0} \setminus \{3\}' is probably Spec over the base S_0, i.e. S_0 − {3} (cf. next page '$S_0 - \{3\}$'); likewise subscripts ρ_0 are likely S_0 / s_0.
'mais de dim 1 en dim 3' is likely 'mais de dim 1 en car 3' (in characteristic 3).
'corr. unim.' is likely 'corr. univ.' or an annotation that G° is the corresponding (unipotent/lattice) part ≃ M; uncertain.
The kernel group written N^{**}_ρ may be a different superscript (struck-out symbol); it is defined as Centr_{G^+}(ρ).
